subject: Electric Supplier Scams and Municipal Climate Updates
overview: The council received a presentation from the Attorney General's Office on predatory third-party electric suppliers and reviewed progress on municipal climate initiatives, including the new high school design and waste management changes.

items.title: Introductions
items.summary: Council members and staff from the Office of Outreach and Prevention introduced themselves and their roles in climate equity and community engagement.

items.title: AGO Presentation on Predatory Electric Suppliers
items.summary: Tiara from the Attorney General’s Office explained how predatory third-party suppliers use deceptive door-to-door and mail marketing to charge residents significantly higher rates than Medford’s municipal aggregation program.

items.title: Medford Community Energy and Coaching Updates
items.summary: Climate Planner Brenda Pike reported that Medford’s community electricity aggregation has saved residents over $12 million compared to basic utility service and provided an update on the city's energy coaching program.

items.title: New High School Sustainability Goals
items.summary: The council reviewed sustainability goals for the new Medford High School, including targeting LEED certification, 100% electrification, and the installation of roof-mounted solar panels.

items.title: Waste Management and Composting Reforms
items.summary: The city announced a plan to transition to bi-weekly trash collection and weekly composting in July 2027, intended to reduce waste volume and promote municipal composting uptake.

items.title: School Solar and Infrastructure Projects
items.summary: Staff reported on a pending solar contract for the McGlynn School and noted that three additional elementary schools have been accepted into a state program for roof repairs and heating upgrades.

items.title: Climate Action Plan Assessment
items.summary: The Energy Environment Committee is currently assessing progress on 171 actions within the city's Climate Action Plan and preparing initiatives for gift-wrapping waste reduction and anti-rodenticide education.

items.title: Administrative Matters
items.summary: The council scheduled its next meeting for January 21, 2026, and deferred the approval of previous meeting minutes until that time.
